newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Benelux says restructuring in effect.
newsitem.headline: Benelux says restructuring in effect.

text.p: Data storage products maker Benelux International Ltd said on Tuesday a capital injection and debt restructuring agreement to solve its liquidity problems was now in effect.

Under the agreement, executed by all parties on January 10, the company proposes to raise about HK$175 million through a rights issue of at least 1.75 billion new shares at HK$0.10 each on the basis of six rights shares for every existing issued share held, Benelux said in a statement.
Prestbury Incorporated Ltd, owned by Indonesian businessman Cahyadi Kumala, also agreed to subscribe for 600 million new shares at HK$0.10 each, it said.
Net proceeds of the rights issue and the subscription were estimated at HK$232 million, it said.
The rights issue and subscription price represents a discount of about 66.7 percent to the stock's last close of HK$0.30 on February 2, 1996, before trading was suspended, the company said.

Benelux said it planned to use about HK$100 million of the proceeds to settle unsecured debt and HK$60 million to repay working capital facilities secured by Prestbury, with the balance as additional working capital.
Benelux said its banks had agreed to a proposal involving the full and final settlement of all unsecured outstanding debt of about HK$500 million on completion of the restructuring.
Benelux, which has been suffering from severe liquidity problems since the begining of 1996, said the proposals were conditional and subject to shareholder approval.
